title: Lexus LX 470
verdict: A 100 Series Land Cruiser with a hydraulic party trick: it rises on its toes to clear a rock, then kneels so you can load the groceries. Keep up with the AHC fluid and the timing belt and it may well outlast the people who sold it new.

paragraphs: The LX 470 is a [[land-cruiser/100-series|100 Series]] Land Cruiser, sharing its floor pan and most of its body panels, with Lexus fitting the expensive suspension from day one. Underneath are a ladder frame, a solid rear axle, torsion-bar independent front suspension, full-time four-wheel drive with a lockable center differential, and Toyota's 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8. On top of that sits Adjustable Height Control (AHC), a hydraulic system that raises the truck for trails and lowers it for loading, plus Adaptive Variable Suspension (AVS) for the dampers. The Land Cruiser didn't get AHC even as an option until 2006. Every LX 470 had it from launch.

story.heading: A V8 AND A NEW FRONT END
paragraphs: Critics had called the [[lexus/lx450|LX 450]] underpowered, so its replacement got a V8. The LX 470 debuted at the Los Angeles Auto Show in December 1997, and sales began in the second quarter of 1998. The 2UZ-FE made 230 hp from launch. It is a quad-cam, 32-valve engine with a timing belt, which shapes the ownership experience. The bigger change was up front. The live axle gave way to independent suspension with torsion bars, a first for the Land Cruiser line, and Wikipedia's Land Cruiser article says that change limited off-road capability and durability.

The lockers went too. The [[lexus/lx450|LX 450]]'s optional electric front and rear lockers disappeared from the US LX. A rear locker stayed available in Canada for 1998 and 1999. In their place came the transfer case's locking center differential and, from 2000, A-TRAC brake-based traction control with VSC. Also in 2000, the front differential went from two pinion gears to four. One IH8MUD veteran warns that pre-2000 front diffs "can grenade with little stress."

story.heading: THE HYDRAULIC TRICK
paragraphs: AHC replaces most of the conventional springing with hydraulics. There are actuators at each corner, gas-charged accumulators (owners call them globes or spheres), a pump and a reservoir. On IH8MUD, owners compare the settings like this: Normal sits at roughly Land Cruiser height, Low is a little over an inch lower, and High is 2–3 inches above a Land Cruiser. AVS picks from 64 damper settings in under 2.5 milliseconds at each wheel, with normal, comfort and sport modes. Both High and Low drop back to Normal above about 20 mph, one owner notes.

It works brilliantly while the fluid is fresh and the globes are charged. Lexus recommends an AHC fluid flush every 60,000 miles, according to the IH8MUD how-to thread, and owners who do it report a dramatically softer ride. When the globes go the ride turns harsh, and the usual test is to watch the reservoir level change between High and Low. Owners also take the cheap way out. They adjust the AHC height sensors for about 2 in of lift, or remove the system entirely and fit conventional springs and shocks, as at least one BaT truck has.

story.heading: YEAR BY YEAR
paragraphs: The LX got the clever features early. The 2001 trucks got DVD navigation and a Mark Levinson option, and in 2002 Night View infrared became an option, a head-up display that projected a thermal image onto the windshield. The 2003 refresh was the big one. It brought a new front end, the A750F five-speed automatic, Variable Gear Ratio Steering, 275/60R18 tires, side curtain airbags, 235 hp and stronger driveshafts with bigger U-joints. For 2006, VVT-i raised output to 275 hp and LED taillights arrived. The last hurrah was a 2007 Limited Edition of 400 trucks in Black Onyx with stone leather.

Not everything aged gracefully. Lexus recalled about 39,000 2003–2007 trucks in 2010 because a hard pothole hit could unseat a snap ring on the steering shaft. The 2UZ also has a habit of loosening its spark plugs, which IH8MUD members have documented in detail. The early tick is often mistaken for a cracked exhaust manifold, which on these engines is also common.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: US sales were 14,732 in calendar 2000 and slid steadily to 2,468 in 2007, when the [[land-cruiser/200-series|200 Series]]-based [[lexus/lx570|LX 570]] arrived with a 383-hp 5.7-liter V8. The LX 470 had collected J.D. Power initial-quality awards (2000, 2002 and 2004) and was named the most reliable luxury SUV over three years in 2005. Its little brother, the [[lexus/gx470|GX 470]], had arrived for 2003 with the same 2UZ-FE V8.

Two decades on, the LX 470 is a bargain for anyone who can wrench. High-mileage trucks with full records are common. IH8MUD signatures list LX 470s past 290,000 miles, and parts, armor and how-tos for the [[land-cruiser/100-series|100 Series]] fit the LX almost without exception. The AHC is the one thing that scares buyers off. Kept up, it's a genuine off-road advantage. If you'd rather not keep it up, the conversion is well documented.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE TOYOTA THAT WAS A LEXUS
callout.title: Land Cruiser Cygnus
paragraphs: In Japan, the LX 470 was sold as a Toyota: the Land Cruiser Cygnus. Wikipedia notes that the 100 Series 'formed the basis for the Lexus LX 470, also sold in Japan as the Toyota Cygnus.' DrivingLine describes the Cygnus as Japan's luxury version of the LX 470.
The Cygnus and the LX shared the gadgets. In 2002, Night View, the infrared camera system that projected a thermal image onto the windshield, arrived on both the Cygnus and the LX 470.

engineering_intro: The LX 470 is built on the UZJ100 ladder frame. It has torsion-bar independent front suspension, a solid rear axle, and full-time 4WD through an HF2A two-speed transfer case with a lockable center differential and no viscous coupler. Lexus added hydraulic Adjustable Height Control and Adaptive Variable Suspension from launch. IH8MUD members note the brakes use a high-pressure pump instead of a vacuum booster, so a brake fault is something to diagnose with a scan tool, not ignore.

engineering.note: Shares the floor pan and most body panels with the 100 Series Land Cruiser.
32-valve quad-cam with a timing belt. VVT-i from 2006. The starter sits under the intake manifold.
Five-speed from 2003. Slee's 100 Series guide says the transmission went sealed (no dipstick) with WS fluid in 2004.
Lockable center diff with no viscous coupler. VSC and A-TRAC from 2000.
Hydraulic height control raises the truck about 2–3 in over Land Cruiser height in High, per owners.
Semi-floating 32-spline rear. Front diff upgraded from 2 to 4 pinions in 2000. Ratio 4.30, then 4.10 from 2003 (Slee, 100 Series).

generations_table.note: Launch. A343F four-speed, 16-in wheels, AHC and AVS standard. Rear locker in Canada only. 2-pinion front diff.
VSC, A-TRAC and brake assist added, plus the stronger 4-pinion front diff. Nav and Mark Levinson from 2001, Night View from 2002.
Facelift. A750F five-speed, VGRS steering, 275/60R18 tires, curtain airbags and stronger driveshafts. Sealed transmission from 2004.
VVT-i and LED taillights. The 2007 Limited Edition was 400 trucks in Black Onyx.

buying_checks.head: AHC health
buying_checks.body: Cycle the truck through Low, Normal and High and watch it level. Look for fluid at the actuators and lines. Check the reservoir level in High and in Low. One IH8MUD member says that if pressures and heights are in spec, a 7-graduation difference means the globes are shot. A harsh, jiggly ride points the same way. Find out when the fluid was last flushed.

buying_checks.head: Timing belt records
buying_checks.body: The 2UZ-FE uses a timing belt with a 90k-mile service. Forum regulars say to confirm the 90k or 180k service has been done if the truck is near those mileages, and to have the water pump, idlers and tensioner done at the same time.

buying_checks.head: Ticks at cold start
buying_checks.body: A tick that fades as the engine warms is often a cracked driver's-side exhaust manifold, which CarSpec calls common on the 2UZ. IH8MUD members warn that the same sound can be a spark plug working loose, so check the plugs before blaming the manifold.

buying_checks.head: Brake warning lights
buying_checks.body: The 100 Series uses a high-pressure brake booster pump and accumulator instead of a vacuum booster. ABS and BRAKE lights plus a warning tone, or a pedal that sinks, mean a scan-tool diagnosis, not a guess. IH8MUD ran a poll on total brake failures, so treat it seriously.

buying_checks.head: Steering and front end
buying_checks.body: Check for power-steering leaks at the rack, play in the steering and torn CV boots. Lexus issued a ball-joint inspection TSB in 2002. Confirm that the 2010 steering-shaft recall (2003–2007 trucks) was done.

buying_checks.head: 1998–1999 throttle gremlins
buying_checks.body: Slee lists accelerator and throttle position sensor faults on 1998–1999 trucks that can leave the truck not responding to the throttle. Make sure the throttle response is clean on the test drive.

buying_checks.head: Rust and use
buying_checks.body: Forum members report plenty of rusty trucks from the northern US. Get underneath with a light. Like any Land Cruiser, a high-mileage truck with full records beats a low-mileage truck with none.

buying_checks.head: Starter health
buying_checks.body: A slow or intermittent crank usually means worn starter contacts. The starter sits under the intake manifold, so it's a big job, and owners usually do it with the timing belt.

repairs.title: AHC fluid flush and bleed
repairs.cost: About 2 cans of Toyota AHC fluid (part 08886-01805, $22/can in 2005) plus about $20 in supplies
repairs.symptoms: A harsh or bouncy ride, dark or metallic-gray fluid in the reservoir, sluggish leveling, or a flush that's overdue (owners say Lexus recommends one every 60k miles).
repairs.fix: Following the IH8MUD how-to: park on level ground, select Low and switch off. Remove the old fluid from the reservoir with a turkey baster or fluid evacuator and refill with new AHC fluid. Fit clear tubing to the bleeder on the driver's front actuator, open it until that corner settles, close it, then start the truck and let it re-level. Repeat for the passenger front, driver rear and passenger rear, topping up as you go. Keep cycling until clean fluid comes out of every corner. Soak the rear bleeders in penetrating oil the day before, because they rust and round off.
repairs.tools: 10 mm wrench · clear tubing · catch bottle · fluid evacuator or turkey baster · penetrating oil · Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805

parts.name: Sway bar refresh kit for AHC trucks (SUS470SBKITAFT)

repairs.title: AHC height-sensor lift
repairs.cost: A can of AHC fluid, scrap aluminum flat stock and an alignment
repairs.symptoms: You want more ground clearance in Normal without giving up AHC.
repairs.fix: Measure the ride height at each corner first. With the ignition off, shorten the front height-sensor links to raise the front about 2 in. Going to 2.5 in means trimming the heim joint, and one side is reverse-threaded. The single rear sensor gives about 1.75 in with its mount slid to the top. More than that needs a 2-in extension bracket. Top up the AHC fluid, do a diff drop if you don't have one, and get an alignment. ATS4X4's advice, quoted in the thread, is to keep at least 70 mm of front droop so the CV boots survive. Lift too far and High mode will refuse to stay up.
repairs.tools: 10 mm socket · cut-off wheel · aluminum flat stock · drill · AHC fluid · tape measure

repairs.title: Timing belt, water pump and 90k service
repairs.time: A weekend (about 15 leisurely hours in one write-up)
repairs.cost: About $600 in parts for a full refresh in one owner's write-up. One owner's 180k service invoice ran about $1,900 in labor, including a snorkel install.
repairs.symptoms: The mileage says 90k, 180k or 270k with no proof the belt was done, or there's a weeping water pump or a rough idler bearing.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant, protect the radiator with cardboard and remove the fan, shroud and belts. Hold the crank and break the crank-pulley bolt loose with a long breaker bar, then pull the pulley. Remove the timing covers, set the timing marks and replace the belt, both idlers, the tensioner, the water pump and the thermostat. Cam and crank seals and radiator hoses are cheap to add. Reassemble, refill and bleed the cooling system. IH8MUD's 90k parts list gives the timing belt as 13568-09070 (check for supersessions).
repairs.tools: ¾-in breaker bar · crank-pulley holder and puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG · drain pan · FSM

parts.name: Timing belt kit with tensioner, UZJ100/LX470 (BELTTKT021)

repairs.title: Starter (or starter contacts) replacement
repairs.time: Big job: the intake manifold has to come off
repairs.cost: Parts plus labor (contacts kit or reman starter)
repairs.symptoms: Clicking or no-crank conditions that come and go and get worse until it won't start.
repairs.fix: The 2UZ's starter lives in the engine's V, under the intake manifold. Disconnect the battery, then remove the intake plumbing and intake manifold, with rags stuffed in the ports so nothing drops into the engine. Unbolt the starter and either rebuild the contacts and plunger or fit a new or reman unit. Owners often do this at the timing-belt halfway point, when the water pump and thermostat housing are out, because access is better.
repairs.tools: Long extensions · magnetic pickup · 22 mm wrench (fuel line) · new intake gaskets · rags

parts.name: Starters and starter parts (2005 LX470 catalog)

repairs.title: Spark plug check and replacement
repairs.cost: A set of 8 plugs (Denso or NGK) plus coil boots
repairs.symptoms: A tick-tick-pop at cold start that can sound like an exhaust leak, a misfire or coil failure. In the worst case a plug blows out of the head and takes the threads with it.
repairs.fix: Blow out the plug wells before loosening anything. Remove the coils, check every plug for tightness and replace them using genuine parts. Don't use anti-seize. Toyota's spec is 13 ft-lb. One veteran IH8MUD poster uses 18 ft-lb. Fit new coil boots and seals and torque the coil bolts to 66 in-lb. He recommends checking the plugs whenever the tick appears and at every timing-belt service.
repairs.tools: Spark plug socket · extensions · torque wrench (in-lb and ft-lb) · compressed air · plugs · coil boots

repairs.title: Exhaust manifold replacement
repairs.time: Same-day job at a specialist shop
repairs.cost: Parts plus labor (high, because the engine mounts must come out)
repairs.symptoms: A tick from the engine bay that's loudest cold and fades as the manifold heats and expands.
repairs.fix: CarSpec found the crack where the flange is welded to the first pipe of the manifold. The fix is a new manifold assembly. The engine mounts have to be released and the engine raised to reach the lower studs, and rusted fasteners are the main fight. Rule out loose spark plugs first.
repairs.tools: Penetrating oil · stud extractor · engine support or jack · new gaskets and studs

parts.name: Exhaust manifolds and studs (2005 LX470 catalog)

repairs.title: Steering rack replacement
repairs.time: A full day, with a friend
repairs.cost: About $530 for a new OEM rack bought through a friend in 2013 (retail $700+), plus coolant, oil, power-steering fluid and an alignment
repairs.symptoms: Power-steering fluid leaking from the rack boots, play in the steering or a heavy feel.
repairs.fix: In the IH8MUD write-up, the oil filter housing comes off first to make room. It has coolant lines, so be ready to catch about half a quart of oil and half a gallon of coolant. Then unbolt the column coupler, both hard lines and the rack mounts, spin the rack off the tie-rod ends and work it out through the frame. Install the new rack centered, reconnect everything, refill and bleed, and get an alignment.
repairs.tools: Long extensions · universal joints · 17 mm line wrench · metric sockets · new oil-filter-housing gasket · rack bushings

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The IH8MUD 100 Series FAQ answer is 285/75R16 or 285/65R18, both about 33 in, with no lift. An owner with a stock '99 found 295/75R16 a tight fit that might not clear at full bump and full lock. Stock sizes were 16-in wheels to 2002 and 275/60R18 from 2003.

faq.q: How much can an LX 470 tow?
What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: The EPA rates a 2002 truck (four-speed) at 12 city, 15 highway and 13 combined. Five-speed trucks are rated 12 city, 15–16 highway and 13 combined. All run on regular fuel.

faq.q: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
faq.a: A belt. The 2UZ-FE is due every 90k miles. Owners replace the water pump, idlers, tensioner and thermostat at the same time, and often the starter or its contacts too, since the intake is already half apart.

If it's healthy, yes. It gives you adjustable ground clearance a spring truck can't match, and a fluid flush is a one-hour job. Owners whose AHC failed have switched to conventional suspension instead. One IH8MUD member went to Old Man Emu 2.5-in heavy springs and called it much cheaper than replacing AHC sensors and actuators, which another member described as very expensive.

faq.q: How do I lift an LX 470?
faq.a: The cheapest way is to adjust the AHC height-sensor links. That gives about 2 in up front (2.5 in with a trimmed heim joint) and about 1.75 in at the rear, or more with an extended bracket. Keep at least 70 mm of front droop for CV boot life, add a diff drop and get an alignment. The other route is removing the AHC and fitting conventional torsion bars, springs and shocks.

US trucks have a lockable center differential, plus brake-based A-TRAC from 2000. A factory rear locker was only offered on Canadian LX 470s in 1998–1999. Aftermarket air lockers are the usual upgrade.

Forum regulars favor 2000 and later for the stronger 4-pinion front differential, and 2003 and later for the A750F five-speed, which one member says makes a big difference. The 2006–2007 trucks add VVT-i and more power. The 2003–2007 trucks should also have had the steering-shaft recall done.

faq.q: What's different from a 100 Series Land Cruiser?
faq.a: The LX has the same drivetrain but different styling and equipment. It had AHC and AVS standard from 1998 (the Land Cruiser only got AHC as an option in 2006), front and rear automatic climate control, a power tilt and telescoping column, projector lows and fogs, body cladding and its own gauges and wheels.

faq.q: Are there recalls I should check?
faq.a: Yes. The big one is the July 2010 recall of about 39,000 2003–2007 LX 470s, which replaced the steering-shaft snap ring and added a retainer. There was also a 2004 US recall that added a resistor to dim daytime running lights that were too bright. In Australia, front rotor bolts and a dash wiring harness were recalled too.

faq.q: What's that tick from the engine?
faq.a: It could be either of two common 2UZ problems. A cracked driver's-side exhaust manifold ticks when cold and fades as it warms. A spark plug working loose makes a similar sound and is far more dangerous, because it can blow out of the head. IH8MUD members recommend checking the plugs first.

mods.why: Adjust the AHC sensors for a lift, refresh the fluid and globes, or convert to conventional springs. Whichever route you take, adjustable rear links keep the rear axle centered once the truck is lifted.

who.name: Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 rear links)

mods.why: The cladding and running boards are expensive to replace. Sliders that bolt to the frame protect the rockers and can still work as steps.
A modular front bumper protects the radiator and carries a winch, which matters on a truck this heavy. A rear bumper with swing-outs moves the spare up and out of the way.
The IFS front differential and the transfer case sit low and exposed.
The stock intake is in the passenger fender. On US-spec trucks Slee notes the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna.
Timing-belt kits, idlers, cam seals and plugs, stocked by people who know the chassis.

baseline_service.intro: Most LX 470s on the market are past at least one 90k service interval, so verify or do the timing belt first. Then flush the AHC fluid, which most owners have never done, and baseline every gear oil. Slee notes the major specs changed in 2003–2004 (five-speed, WS fluid, long-life coolant), so check which side of the line your truck falls on.
